title: BasePart.Touched
summary: Fires when another part makes physical contact with this part — passes the OTHER part. The trigger behind kill bricks, pads, pickups; fires multiple times per character (each touching limb), so debounce.

parameters.name: otherPart
parameters.description: The part that touched this one — often a character limb. Check its Parent for the character/model.

details.heading: Requirements
details.body: Requires CanTouch = true on this part and actual physics contact (CanCollide isn't strictly required — non-colliding parts can still touch if overlapping). Fires for every touching part, repeatedly.

details.heading: TouchEnded
details.body: The companion event for when contact stops.

explanation.whatItIs: The 'something bumped me' sensor on every part.
explanation.whyItExists: Contact-based gameplay — lava, bounce pads, finish lines, pickups — needs a physical trigger.
whenNotToUse: Precise hit registration for weapons — raycasts or server validation
When nothing physical should trigger it (use ProximityPrompt/ClickDetector)
tips: A walking character touches with multiple parts — expect 2-6 fires; debounce or make effects idempotent
CanTouch=false disables it without removing the handler
commonMistakes: Rewarding each limb touch — players get 5x coins (debounce!)
Trusting client-side Touched for damage — authority belongs on the server
Forgetting the event passes the OTHER part, not a player

examples.title: Debounced bounce pad
examples.code:
local pad = script.Parent
local lastTouch = {}

pad.Touched:Connect(function(otherPart)
    local character = otherPart.Parent
    local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if not humanoid then return end

    local now = os.clock()
    if lastTouch[character] and now - lastTouch[character] < 1 then
        return   -- debounce: one bounce per second per character
    end
    lastTouch[character] = now

    local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
    if root then
        root.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.new(0, 120, 0)
    end
end)
examples.whyItWorks: The table tracks last-bounce time per character, collapsing the multiple limb touches into one action.
examples.commonMistake: Without the debounce table, every limb contact re-launches the player mid-air.
